Definition: middle voice from the base of G4756; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations:--soldier, (go to) war(-fare).
BiblicalUsage: To serve as a soldier is to war, and the word is used of the ministry and of the heart. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please him who chose him to be a soldier; who goeth a warfare at his own charges? And James asks whence come wars among you, and whether they come of your lusts that war in your members.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the soldier's life is the Christian's: unentangled, at another's charges, and at war first with his own lusts.
